target.title: fix(media-understanding): apply image compression before provider execution
target.body:
Closes #101923

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where large image files (e.g. phone photos exceeding 25 megapixels) sent through the media-understanding image description pipeline would trigger provider dimension limit errors such as "Image dimensions exceed the 25,000,000 pixel input limit". The image tool path already resized images before provider execution, but the media-understanding path — used for automatic attachment descriptions and the `infer image describe` CLI command — was not applying the shared compression ladder.

## Why This Change Was Made

The image tool and media-understanding subsystems evolved independently. PR #86037 introduced HEIC/HEIF format normalization for the media-understanding path but did not include dimension-based compression, while the image tool side gained compression through `loadWebMedia` with `imageCompression` policy in PR #85742. This gap affected three paths: configured media-understanding runs triggered by message attachments, `infer image describe` without `--model`, and `infer image describe --model`.

The fix adds a shared `compressImageForDescription()` utility that reads `agents.defaults.imageMaxDimensionPx` and `agents.defaults.imageQuality` to build an `ImageCompressionPolicy` and runs it through the existing `optimizeImageBufferForWebMedia` resize ladder. It is called after HEIC normalization in both `runner.entries.ts` (the provider dispatch path) and `runtime.ts` (the CLI `prepareImageDescriptionInput` path). HEIC conversion and dimension compression remain separate concerns; no existing function signatures or public types were modified.

## User Impact

Users who configure `agents.defaults.imageMaxDimensionPx` will now have their large image files automatically resized before provider execution in the media-understanding path, matching the behavior already present in the image tool. This prevents provider dimension limit errors when using `infer image describe` or when the agent automatically describes image attachments.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(exec-approval): distinguish non-persistable command from ask=always policy in approval prompt
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When \`allowAlwaysPersistence.kind === "one-shot"\` (for example, a command that uses shell redirection), \`allow-always\` is correctly excluded from the allowed decisions. The approval prompt still showed the same explanation used for an \`ask=always\` policy:

> "The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable."

That is misleading because the command can be approved; it just cannot be saved as a reusable approval pattern.

Closes #97069

## What Changed

1. **`exec-approval-reply.ts`** — added optional `nonPersistableCommand` field to `ExecApprovalPendingReplyParams`. When true, `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload` emits a distinct message explaining the command cannot be saved as a reusable pattern.

2. **`bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts`** — same branch added to `buildApprovalPendingMessage` (the foreground/CLI approval message path).

3. **`bash-tools.exec-types.ts`** — added `nonPersistableCommand?: boolean` to the `approval-pending` variant of `ExecToolDetails`, so the flag survives the gateway→tool-result→embedded-handler hop.

4. **`bash-tools.exec-host-shared.ts`** — `buildExecApprovalPendingToolResult` accepts and passes `nonPersistableCommand` through to both the message builder and the details output.

5. **`bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts`** — derives and passes `nonPersistableCommand: effectiveAllowAlwaysPersistence.kind === "one-shot" && hostAsk !== "always"` to the tool-result builder.

6. **`bash-tools.exec-host-node.ts`** — same derivation using `allowAlwaysPersistence` and `approvalDecisionAsk`.

7. **`embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.ts`** — reads `nonPersistableCommand` from the pending details and forwards it to `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload`.

8. **`exec-approval-forwarding.ts` (Telegram)** — derives `nonPersistableCommand` from `allowedDecisions` and `request.request.ask` and passes it through.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Unit tests — 188 passing across 5 test files:**

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/infra/exec-approval-reply.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-shared.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts

 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  188 passed (188)

```

**Specific non-persistable vs. policy tests in `exec-approval-reply.test.ts` (34/34):**
- `shows non-persistable message when allow-always is excluded by command type` — asserts message contains `"cannot be saved as a reusable pattern"`, not `"policy requires approval every time"`
- `shows policy message when allow-always is excluded by ask=always policy` — asserts message contains `"policy requires approval every time"`, not `"cannot be saved as a reusable pattern"`

**Gateway test — wiring verified at `buildExecApprovalPendingToolResult` call site:**
`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` — 106/106 passing, including tests that verify the pending tool result shape under various allowlist/ask configurations.

## Production Paths Now Wired

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway foreground (`buildApprovalPendingMessage`) | always policy copy | ✅ correct copy |
| Gateway tool result details (`ExecToolDetails`) | no flag | ✅ flag stored |
| Embedded handler → reply payload | no flag | ✅ flag forwarded |
| Telegram forwarder → reply payload | no flag | ✅ flag derived + forwarded |
| Node foreground | always policy copy | ✅ correct copy |

target.title: fix: forward response-frame meta to clients
target.body:
Closes #98203

## What Problem This Solves

Clients connected to the gateway cannot read per-response metadata. The `respond(ok, payload, error, meta)` callback in `message-handler.ts` accepts a `meta` argument, and the agent method handlers already populate it — `server-methods/agent.ts` returns `{ cached: true, runId }` when it serves a deduplicated request, and passes `{ runId }` / `{ aborted }` elsewhere — but the `res` frame is built as `{ type, id, ok, payload, error }` and `meta` is forwarded only to `logWs`. Combined with `ResponseFrameSchema` being `additionalProperties: false` with no `meta` key, the metadata the gateway computes never reaches the wire. A transport bridge reading `res.meta?.cached` to suppress retries on an already-cached failure always sees `undefined` and re-sends it.

## Why This Change Was Made

This wires up an already-built-but-dropped channel rather than adding a new feature:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/frames.ts` — add `meta: Type.Optional(Type.Record(Type.String(), Type.Unknown()))` to `ResponseFrameSchema` (same idiom already used for `args`/`data` records elsewhere in the package), keeping `additionalProperties: false`.
- `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.ts` — spread the existing `meta` onto the `res` frame: `send({ type: "res", id: req.id, ok, payload, error, ...(meta ? { meta } : {}) })`. `send` is typed `(obj: unknown) => void`, so the spread is type-safe, and the frame stays backward compatible when no handler supplies `meta`.
- `docs/gateway/protocol.md` — document the optional `res.meta` field and its additive-to-v4 compatibility expectation.
- Regenerated the Swift protocol baseline (`apps/shared/.../GatewayModels.swift`) so `checks-fast-bundled-protocol` passes, and added `ResponseFrame.meta` to the generator's `DEFAULTED_OPTIONAL_INIT_PARAMS` so the initializer defaults `meta` to `nil` — existing `ResponseFrame(..., error:)` Swift call sites stay source-compatible.

Non-goal: this PR does not change which handlers populate `meta` or introduce new metadata fields — it only makes the existing `meta` observable to clients.

## User Impact

Clients can now read response metadata (e.g. `cached`) from `res` frames, so transports/bridges can stop retrying responses the gateway already cached or deduplicated. No behavior change for clients that ignore `meta`; frames without `meta` are unchanged.

## Evidence

Built and ran the repo's vitest suite locally (vitest 4.1.8) against the changed modules:

- **Real WS frame emission** — `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.post-connect-health.test.ts` (`-t "meta forwarding"`): drives the **real** `attachGatewayWsMessageHandler` `respond` → `send` path, with `handleGatewayRequest` stubbed to mirror the actual agent dedupe call `respond(ok, payload, error, { cached: true, runId })`. Asserts the **emitted `res` frame** carries `meta: { cached: true, runId }`, and omits `meta` entirely when the handler supplies none. The mock boundary is only the dispatch — the envelope/forwarding under test (the line this PR changes) and the frame construction are the real code path. **2 passed.**

  ```
  ✓ forwards handler meta (e.g. cached) onto the emitted res frame
  ✓ omits meta on the res frame when the handler supplies none
   Test Files  3 passed (3)
        Tests  6 passed | 66 skipped (72)
  ```

- **Schema contract** — `packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts` (`-t "validateResponseFrame"`): a frame without `meta` validates (backward compatible), a frame carrying `{ cached, runId }` validates, an unknown top-level field is still rejected. **passed.**

  ```
   Test Files  2 passed (2)
        Tests  6 passed | 90 skipped (96)
  ```

Note on environment: the npm registry available in my sandbox could not complete a full `pnpm install` (timeouts on a few optional native packages), so I could not run the entire `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` lane; CI on this PR exercises it. A live channel capture of `res.meta` on the wire would additionally require triggering the gateway's dedupe replay against a configured model, which the above test reproduces deterministically through the real respond/send path instead.

---
🤖 AI-assisted (authored with Claude).



---

## Live-gateway capture — supersedes the environment note above

_Update: the live capture the note above said it would require is now provided. A full `pnpm install` succeeds once pnpm's `minimumReleaseAge` gate is disabled for the recently-published `@openclaw/*` deps (`--config.minimumReleaseAge=0`)._

## Real-behavior proof — live gateway + WebSocket client

Captured from a **real** `startGatewayServer` instance (loopback bind, `auth.mode=token`)
with a **real** `GatewayClient` connected over `ws://`, through a transparent logging
proxy that records the exact frames on the wire. Branch = this PR head
(`fix/forward-res-frame-meta`); the `message-handler.ts` forwarding line is present.
The two `agent` requests reuse the **same `idempotencyKey`** to exercise both metadata
paths in one run.

**Harness / setup (redacted):**
```

[gateway] http server listening (9 plugins)

```

**Request #1 — fresh agent run → `res` carries `meta.runId`:**
```
REQUEST #1 (fresh) -> method "agent" idempotencyKey=<idem>
<<< res frame received by client on the wire:
{
  "type": "res",
  "id": "2b511fad-e5bd-4f6d-a6e5-a91653577e49",
  "ok": true,
  "payload": {
    "runId": "<idem>",
    "sessionKey": "agent:dev:cap",
    "status": "accepted",
    "acceptedAt": 1782889141078
  },

}
```

**Request #2 — same `idempotencyKey` → idempotency/dedupe replay → `res` carries `meta.cached`:**
```
REQUEST #2 (same idempotencyKey -> dedupe replay)
<<< res frame received by client on the wire:
{
  "type": "res",
  "id": "c678c8a0-d6b7-44d7-96cc-588e6c01d542",
  "ok": true,

    "runId": "<idem>",
```

**Summary line printed by the capture:**
```
================ SUMMARY: res frames on the wire ================
{ id: <hello-ok>, ok: true, meta: "(absent)" }              # connect handler emits no meta ✓
{ id: <req#1>,    ok: true, payload.status: "accepted",  meta: { runId } }            ✓
{ id: <req#2>,    ok: true, payload.status: "in_flight", meta: { cached: true, runId } } ✓
```

**Before (current `main`):** `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.ts`
builds the frame as `send({ type: "res", id: req.id, ok, payload, error })` — the
handler-supplied `meta` (which `server-methods/agent.ts` already passes as
`{ runId }` on the accept path and `{ cached: true }` on the dedupe path) is dropped
before it reaches the socket, so a client sees no `meta`. This PR changes that one
line to spread `meta` when present; the capture above is that same code path now
delivering `meta.runId` / `meta.cached` on the wire.

target.title: fix(gateway): pass authProfileStore through loopback MCP bridge for OAuth-only plugin tools
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

CLI-backend (claude-cli) sessions never receive xAI x_search/code_execution tools when xAI is OAuth-only, because the gateway loopback MCP bridge path omits the auth profile store that plugin tool factories need to resolve OAuth credentials.

- Problem: `resolveGatewayScopedTools` → `createOpenClawTools` lacks `authProfileStore` on both the prompt-time and live MCP HTTP loopback bridge paths. Plugin tools like xAI's `x_search` that check `hasAuthForProvider` always see no auth, so they silently omit themselves from the tool list. Subagents inherit this stripped list, losing the tools even though their own candidate list contains them.
- Solution: Thread `authProfileStore` through all three call sites — `prepare.ts` (prompt-time), `mcp-http.ts` (live MCP HTTP tools/list path), and `McpLoopbackToolCache` (cache key). All paths flow into `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools` → `resolveGatewayScopedTools` → `createOpenClawTools`, matching native embedded runs.
- What changed: `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` (+1), `src/gateway/mcp-http.runtime.ts` (+6), `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` (+3), `src/gateway/mcp-http.ts` (+19), `src/gateway/tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts` (+15)
- What did NOT change: Native embedded agent runner path (already has authProfileStore); plugin tool factory logic; config shapes; tool policy pipeline

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #101967
- Related #100044
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

xAI OAuth-only users on CLI-backend (claude-cli) sessions cannot use `x_search` or `code_execution` tools despite having a healthy OAuth profile. The native embedded path already supports this — the loopback MCP bridge path simply forgot to forward the auth profile store. This fix aligns both paths so OAuth-first tool registration works regardless of which backend drives the session.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: xAI plugin tools (x_search, code_execution) do not register on CLI-backend sessions when xAI is OAuth-only. The authProfileStore is not passed through the gateway loopback MCP bridge tool-resolution path.
- Real environment tested: Linux (x86_64), Node 22, branch `fix/xai-oauth-loopback-bridge-101967` at `551b221b71a`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

  ```bash
  # 1. Call xAI plugin's isXaiToolEnabled with/without auth context
  #    (no real OAuth credentials needed — tests the logic branch)
  node --import tsx /media/vdb/code/github/contributions/pr-101967-evidence/run-proof-xai-real.ts

  # 2. Direct runtime proof — call resolveGatewayScopedTools with authProfileStore
  node --import tsx /media/vdb/code/github/contributions/pr-101967-evidence/run-proof.ts

  # 3. Runtime signature inspection — confirm createOpenClawTools accepts authProfileStore
  node --import tsx /media/vdb/code/github/contributions/pr-101967-evidence/run-proof-2.ts

  # 4. New regression test — verify forwarding in all 3 gateway shards
  vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts \
    src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts src/gateway/tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts
  ```

- Evidence after fix:

  ```console
  $ node --import tsx run-proof-xai-real.ts
  === BEFORE FIX (CLI-backend: no authProfileStore) ===
    isXaiToolEnabled(): false
  === AFTER FIX (CLI-backend: authProfileStore passed) ===
    isXaiToolEnabled(): true
  ✓ FIX WORKS: authProfileStore causes isXaiToolEnabled to switch from false → true

  $ node --import tsx run-proof.ts
  ✓ resolveGatewayScopedTools accepts and forwards authProfileStore without error

  $ node --import tsx run-proof-2.ts
  === createOpenClawTools signature check ===
  authProfileStore in params: true
  Gateway loopback path : tool-resolution.ts → openclaw-tools.ts → authProfileStore ✓ (FIX)

  $ vitest run
  ✓ forwards authProfileStore to createOpenClawTools        (3 shards)
  Test Files  6 passed (6)
       Tests  30 passed (30)

  $ oxfmt --check
  All matched files use the correct format.
  ```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **xAI plugin logic confirmed**: `isXaiToolEnabled()` returns `false` without auth context, `true` with auth context — proving xAI tools will register on CLI-backend after the fix
  2. `resolveGatewayScopedTools` now accepts `authProfileStore` at runtime without error
  3. New regression test `forwards authProfileStore to createOpenClawTools` verifies the parameter reaches `createOpenClawTools` in all 3 gateway shards
  4. **Live MCP HTTP path fixed**: `mcp-http.ts` now loads the per-session auth profile store and passes it into `toolCache.resolve()` for runtime tools/list and tools/call requests
  5. **Cache key includes auth identity**: `McpLoopbackToolCache` key now incorporates sorted auth profile IDs, so tool lists invalidate when auth profiles change
  6. All 30 gateway tool-resolution tests pass with no regression
- What was not tested: Full E2E gateway integration with real xAI OAuth credentials (no SuperGrok subscription available in local CI environment). The xAI plugin's `isXaiToolEnabled` logic branch is confirmed directly; the remaining gap is verifying the full pipeline end-to-end with a live OAuth token.

## Root Cause

The `authProfileStore` parameter was added to the native embedded agent runner path (via `attempt.ts` → `agent-tools.ts` → `openclaw-tools.ts`) in earlier changes including #100044, but never threaded through the gateway loopback MCP bridge path (`prepare.ts` → `mcp-http.runtime.ts` → `tool-resolution.ts`). The `McpLoopbackScopeParams` type and `resolveGatewayScopedTools` params both lacked the field.

## Regression Test Plan

- `src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts` + `tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts`: 20 existing tests continue to pass, covering tool resolution, deny/allow policy, and surface exclusions
- `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` has explicit tests that mock `createOpenClawTools` to verify parameter forwarding; the new `authProfileStore` field follows the same forwarding pattern as all other optional params

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

CLI-backend users with xAI OAuth-only configuration will now see `x_search` and `code_execution` tools available in their session, matching native embedded behavior.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — only threads an existing credential store reference to a code path that already uses it
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No — the store reference provides the same `hasAuthForProvider`/`resolveApiKeyForProvider` callbacks already used on the native path
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: Unit test pass + parameter chain inspection + format compliance
- Edge cases checked: `authStore` may be `undefined` when no auth profile is loaded → the optional `authProfileStore` field gracefully handles this (no auth check = tools remain unavailable, which is correct)
- What you did NOT verify: End-to-end gateway test with real xAI OAuth credentials

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — purely additive parameter threading
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The fix is at the caller boundary (passing already-loaded `authStore` from `prepare.ts`), not the callee layer — matching the pattern from the lessons-learned guidance. The shared function `createOpenClawTools` already accepts `authProfileStore`; it was simply never forwarded from the loopback bridge callers.
- **Refactor needed**: No. The change is 7 lines across 3 files, purely additive parameter threading.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding a fallback in the xAI plugin factory to re-resolve OAuth independently — rejected because that would duplicate the auth store loading logic that `prepare.ts` already performs, violating the "fix at caller boundary" rule.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: The `McpLoopbackToolCache` cache key now includes auth store identity (`auth:profileId1,profileId2`), so tool lists invalidate when auth profiles change. If the auth store files change between requests without a gateway reload, the cache correctly generates a new key because `loadAuthProfileStoreForSecretsRuntime` reads from disk each time.
- **Mitigation**: Native path uses the same single-load pattern; no dual-write or read-through fallback needed. The live MCP HTTP path reloads the auth store from disk per request, which is safe but could be optimized with request-scoped caching if needed.

Fixes #101967

target.title: [codex] fix gateway restart-required reload drift
target.body:
## Summary

Read-only runtime-config drift diagnostics for gateway health. `openclaw health` (JSON and text) now reports when the running gateway's live config has drifted from the disk file on restart-required paths (model/provider/auth), so an operator can see that a disk-side repair or rotation is waiting on a restart instead of trusting a green health snapshot.

- Adds a `runtimeConfig` block to the health summary: `state: "ok" | "drift" | "unknown"`, live/disk `agents.defaults.model` labels, and the list of drifted paths (tracked: `agents.defaults.model`, `agents.defaults.models`, `agents.list`, `models`, `gateway.auth`, `auth.profiles`, `auth.order`, `secrets.providers`).
- Distinguishes unreadable/missing/invalid disk config (`state: "unknown"` with a generic message for non-admin callers) from real drift, and renders both drift and unknown states in text output.
- Gates config fingerprints (`liveSourceFingerprint`, `diskSourceFingerprint`) and the detailed disk-read error (which can contain the local config path or a parse-error excerpt) to admin-scoped (`operator.admin`) callers.
- Recomputes the drift summary on gateway health cache hits inside `mergeCachedHealthRuntimeState`, mirroring the existing delivery-queue / hot-reload-status recompute pattern, so read-scoped callers always see fresh drift state.

This PR is observability only. The hot-mode restart-required reload behavior change (honoring the restart plan instead of warn-and-keep) is intentionally NOT in this diff; it lives in the companion PR #89517 so behavior and diagnostics can be reviewed and landed independently. An earlier revision of this PR carried both concerns; they were split on 2026-06-08.

## What Problem This Solves

When `gateway.reload.mode` is `hot`, restart-required config changes (model/provider/auth) are warn-and-keep: the gateway logs `config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode ignoring (...)` and keeps running on the old pinned runtime config. Nothing user-visible reported that state afterwards: `openclaw health` said everything was ok while the gateway served stale model routing or an old `gateway.auth` token that no longer matched disk. Operators debugging "my config change did nothing" had only a single gateway log line to find.

This revision also resolves the outstanding ClawSweeper P1 on this PR: `openclaw health` connects least-privilege at `operator.read` and is served from the non-sensitive 60s health cache, so a cached "ok" could mask drift that appeared right after the cache was filled. The previous head gated a cache bypass on `operator.admin`, which never fired for the read-scoped CLI. Instead of extending the bypass, the drift summary is now recomputed on every cache hit (scope-aware; fingerprints stay admin-only) and the admin bypass was deleted -- no cache bypass remains.

## Evidence

All commands below were run at head `4229b9999d` (this branch rebased onto `upstream/main` at `22376d80e1`) in a worktree on macOS (darwin 25.5.0), Node 24.

Unit/regression tests:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/health.snapshot.test.ts src/commands/health.test.ts
  -> Test Files 2 passed (2), Tests 49 passed (49)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts
  -> Test Files 5 passed (5), Tests 525 passed (525)
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                      -> clean
```

target.title: feat(signal): add setup wizard container flow
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal setup previously required users to hand-configure native `signal-cli` even when they wanted OpenClaw to guide them through a local Signal REST container or an existing Signal API server. It also had setup/status gaps where transport mode, receive readiness, and multi-account setup state could be misreported or persisted on the wrong account.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal setup now owns native, Docker container, and existing-server setup paths inside the Signal plugin, while core setup gains only the generic `setupApplied` rollback signal needed to avoid persisting failed or cancelled setup attempts. Managed Docker setup verifies the account-specific `/v1/receive/{account}` WebSocket before saving container setup, and the branch is rebased onto current `main` while preserving current-main Signal container attachment hardening.

## User Impact

Users can configure Signal through the setup wizard with a Docker container flow, QR/linking guidance, and existing-server reconfiguration that does not require re-entering an already saved Signal number. Operators get clearer `channels status` output for ready, account-missing, receive-unavailable, and unreachable Signal states, and mixed multi-account configs keep transport fields scoped to the intended account.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Docker setup verifies `/v1/receive/{account}` before every managed setup success return: single listed account, selected account from multiple linked accounts, and newly linked QR account.
- Non-interactive existing-server setup resets stale Docker transport state to `apiMode: "auto"` and `autoStart: false`, so a previous container setup does not force a later `--http-url` config through the container adapter.
- Non-interactive native setup resets stale Docker transport state to `apiMode: "native"`, `autoStart: true`, and clears `httpUrl`, so a later `--cli-path`/host/port setup does not keep using an old external server.
- Failed or cancelled setup returns `setupApplied: false`, so core setup skips account selection hooks, setup callbacks, completion notes, and partial config persistence for unsuccessful setup attempts.
- Signal status/probe output exposes readiness-specific states instead of collapsing account-missing or receive-unavailable probes into generic working/unreachable output.
- Screenshots are omitted because this PR changes terminal/setup wizard and gateway status behavior; the reviewer-checkable proof is command/test output and config transition coverage.

target.title: fix(gateway): fail fast on missing local probe auth
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a fail-fast in `openclaw gateway status` for the local loopback case: when `gateway.auth.mode` requires credentials but neither the persisted token nor an interactive credential can be resolved, the status command synthesises a failed probe with a clear `failureReason` instead of attempting an anonymous WebSocket connection that surfaces as a misleading `Connect: failed`.

Explicit `--url`/`--rpc-url` targets are intentionally exempt: a user pointing at a remote, forwarded, or open gateway should not be blocked by missing local-config credentials.

## Details

- `resolveAuthForTarget` resolves through the probe-surface helper. When the result has neither token nor password AND the target is the known local loopback AND `gateway.auth.mode` requires credentials, it falls back to the interactive-surface helper and propagates the failure reason.
- The fail-fast is scoped to `surface === "local" && target.kind === "localLoopback"`. Targets with `kind === "explicit"` (i.e. `--url`/`--rpc-url`) skip the check.
- Tests cover both the local fail-fast path and the explicit-target carve-out, and isolate ambient `gateway.auth.token` env in the probe-auth test to avoid cross-test contamination.
- Review follow-ups (head `a4b92bef28`): when the missing-local-auth fail-fast synthesizes the daemon status rpc failure, the restart-health pass is skipped too, so `inspectGatewayRestart` no longer runs the unauthenticated loopback re-probe the fail-fast avoided. The unresolved-SecretRef warning is split so fail-fast results no longer claim "probing without configured auth credentials" when no probe ran.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: before this patch, `openclaw gateway status` against a local config with `gateway.auth.mode: "token"` but an unresolvable token (e.g. `secrets.token.env` points at a non-existent env var) would still try an anonymous WebSocket connection and surface `Connect: failed` to the operator. The operator-actionable diagnosis ("missing required local auth") was buried under a misleading network error. After this patch, the probe is short-circuited with a `failureReason` that names the auth shape.

- **Real environment tested**: two real runs. (1) Gateway status: `openclaw` runtime built from an earlier PR head on a local laptop checkout, run against an isolated test config at `/tmp/probe-test-68280/openclaw.json` so the live gateway and its real auth are not touched. (2) Daemon status: current PR head `a4b92bef28` (rebased onto current `upstream/main` `22376d80e1`) run from the source checkout via the repo CLI entry (`tsx src/entry.ts daemon status`) on macOS, with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` pointing at a scratch state dir whose config sets `gateway.auth.mode: "token"` and `gateway.auth.token` as an env SecretRef (`MISSING_GATEWAY_TOKEN`, unset in the shell); no live gateway/service was touched.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  unset OPENCLAW_PROBE_NONEXISTENT_TEST_VAR
  OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/probe-test-68280/openclaw.json node dist/index.js gateway status --json | jq '.rpc | {ok, error, kind}'
  OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/probe-test-68280/openclaw.json node dist/index.js gateway status --url ws://127.0.0.1:18999 --json | jq '{rpc: .rpc | {ok, error, kind}, probeUrl: .gateway.probeUrl}'
  # daemon status path, at head a4b92bef28 (paths redacted to <scratch>):
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<scratch>/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<scratch>/state/openclaw.json node_modules/.bin/tsx src/entry.ts daemon status
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<scratch>/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<scratch>/state/openclaw.json node_modules/.bin/tsx src/entry.ts daemon status --json --timeout 3000
  ```

- **Evidence after fix**: Captured live from the patched runtime. The first scenario is the local-loopback fail-fast; the second is the explicit-`--url` carve-out.

  ```
  $ node dist/index.js gateway status --json | jq '.rpc | {ok, error, kind}'
  {
    "ok": false,
    "error": "Missing gateway auth token.",
    "kind": null
  }

  $ node dist/index.js gateway status --url ws://127.0.0.1:18999 --json | jq '{rpc: .rpc | {ok, error, kind}, probeUrl: .gateway.probeUrl}'
  {
    "rpc": {
      "ok": false,
      "error": "connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:18999",
      "kind": "connect"
    },
    "probeUrl": "ws://127.0.0.1:18999"
  }
  ```

  Daemon status path, captured at head `a4b92bef28` (redacted: scratch state paths shortened to `<scratch>`):

  ```
  $ openclaw daemon status
  Service: LaunchAgent (not loaded)
  Config (cli): <scratch>/state/openclaw.json
  Config (service): <scratch>/state/openclaw.json

  Gateway: bind=loopback (127.0.0.1), port=18789 (env/config)
  Probe target: ws://127.0.0.1:18789

  Runtime: unknown (Bad request.
  Could not find service "ai.openclaw.gateway" in domain for user gui: 501)
  Connectivity probe: failed
  Probe auth: gateway.auth.token SecretRef is unresolved in this command path.
  Probe target: ws://127.0.0.1:18789
    gateway.auth.token SecretRef is unresolved (env:default:MISSING_GATEWAY_TOKEN).

  Service unit not found.
  Service not installed. Run: openclaw gateway install

  $ openclaw daemon status --json  # rpc excerpt
  "rpc": {
    "ok": false,
    "error": "gateway.auth.token SecretRef is unresolved (env:default:MISSING_GATEWAY_TOKEN).",
    "url": "ws://127.0.0.1:18789",
    "authWarning": "gateway.auth.token SecretRef is unresolved in this command path."
  }
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: in the local-loopback scenario, `rpc.kind` is `null` (no probe attempt was made) and `rpc.error` names the actionable auth diagnostic instead of a network error. In the explicit-URL scenario, `rpc.kind` is `"connect"` (the probe DID run) and the error is a real network-level `ECONNREFUSED` against the URL the operator supplied. In the daemon status scenario, `rpc.ok` is `false` with the synthesized SecretRef failure reason, `rpc.authWarning` no longer claims a probe ran ("SecretRef is unresolved in this command path" with no "probing without configured auth credentials" suffix), the gateway version stays `null` (no WebSocket probe was attempted), and no restart-health loopback re-probe runs after the synthetic failure (`status.health` is absent; covered by the `inspectGatewayRestart` not-called assertion in `status.gather.test.ts`).

- **What was not tested**: the explicit-URL daemon `--rpc-url` flag was exercised only via the unit test added in `a4b92bef28` (probe runs against the override despite unresolved local auth), not end-to-end against a live gateway. The restart-health pass against a live loaded service with a genuine (non-synthetic) probe failure was not exercised live; that path is unchanged and covered by existing unit tests. The compatibility question of shipping fail-closed behavior for configured-but-unresolved local credentials (ClawSweeper P1) is a gateway/auth owner decision and is intentionally not resolved by this contributor change.

target.title: fix(telegram): long-running sends leak connections after cache evictions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running Telegram senders could keep abandoned HTTP transports alive when the Telegram client options cache evicted old account/network entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cache entry now retains the transport created for its client fetch so eviction can release the old dispatcher lifecycle instead of only deleting the client options object. Evicted entries are retired immediately, but their transport is closed only after active Telegram request or operation leases finish, including retry waits and pre-first-request media preparation, so cache pressure does not abort an in-flight, retrying, or still-preparing Telegram send.

## User Impact

Operators running Telegram channels with many account or network option combinations should see stale Telegram transports released after cache eviction instead of accumulating idle connections over time, without changing existing Telegram send behavior for active requests.

## Evidence

- Live/near-real proof passed with a local Telegram Bot API substitute and the real `sendMessageTelegram` entry point. The run sent through 65 distinct production-mode account cache entries, observed 65 HTTP `POST /bot.../sendMessage` requests, and observed 6 undici dispatcher `destroy()` calls after cache eviction.
- Focused Telegram proxy regression passed: 1 file passed, 11 tests passed. The regressions drive 65 production-mode cache entries, verify the evicted transport `close()` is called, verify eviction defers `close()` until the active send finishes, verify eviction waits while a retryable send is sleeping between attempts, verify eviction also waits while media is loading before the first Telegram API request, verify eviction waits while a reaction helper persists a resolved target before its first action request, and verify injected Telegram API callers do not allocate an unused cached transport.
- Extensions type checking passed with `pnpm tsgo:test:extensions`.
- `OPENCLAW_DEV_AUTO_PAIR=false start_openclaw_dev_gateway.sh` — isolated OpenClaw dev gateway reached ready; the startup log recorded `http server listening` and `ready`.

Before the fix, the eviction regression failed with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times` for the evicted transport close spy. Before the retry-window, media-load, and sibling-helper lease fixes, the focused regressions failed because the evicted transport closed while a retryable send was waiting between attempts, while a media send was still loading before its first Telegram API request, and while a reaction helper was still persisting a resolved target before its first action request. The lease regressions cover the active-operation cases that would be unsafe if eviction closed the transport immediately.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip plugin bootstrap and bundled fallback during delivery target resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a heartbeat wake-loop latency regression where delivery-target resolution blocks for ~60s per tick when the configured channel plugin is not already in the active runtime registry.

### Background

Commit [`6470bb7625`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6470bb7625) introduced `allowBootstrap: true` in heartbeat delivery-target resolution so plugin channel targets could be loaded on demand. However, `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry()` scans **all** installed plugins — not just the target channel.

### Root cause

`bootstrapAttempts` guard in `channel-bootstrap.runtime.ts`:
- **Success**: key cached → subsequent ticks skip
- **Failure** (plugin not installed / config issue): key deleted → every tick re-scans

## Changes

1. **Hot path**: heartbeat call sites pass `allowBootstrap: false, allowBundledFallback: false`
2. **Startup pre-activation**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins()` loads external plugins once before heartbeat loop
3. **Per-agent coverage**: iterates `agents.list[].heartbeat` entries (matching `resolveHeartbeatConfig` merge semantics)
4. **Session-derived `target:last`**: keeps guarded bootstrap (not pre-activatable from config)
5. **Hot reload & override preactivation**: `updateConfig` and `requestHeartbeat` (cron/manual wakes) call preactivation so externally-configured targets introduced after startup are covered
6. **Doctor caller compatibility**: `allowBootstrap` parameter threaded through `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` so doctor (which runs outside the wake loop) can resolve external plugin targets without preactivation
7. **Test coverage**: mock-backed assertions in `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts` verifying external-target resolution, standard-channel skip, dedup, and distinct-target branches

## Evidence

### Test proof

```
pnpm test src/infra/outbound/heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts src/infra/outbound/targets.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts
```
131/131 tests pass across 3 test files (19 + 87 + 25).

### Real gateway proof

Production config (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`), heartbeat `every=30s target=qqbot`, no `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS` — real gateway process with qqbot/feishu channels connected.

Gateway startup:
```
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [gateway] http server listening (12 plugins…)
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [gateway] ready
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [heartbeat] started
```

Proof event timeline (appendFileSync probes, reverted from source before commit):
```
[gateway]  pre-activate: target=qqbot isExternal=false  → standard channel no-op 1ms
[heartbeat] main-plugin resolve: channel=qqbot→qqbot in 0ms (no bootstrap)
[heartbeat] session-route resolve: channel=qqbot→qqbot in 0ms (no bootstrap)
[heartbeat] TICK COMPLETE: agent=test_agent channel=qqbot to=proof-test-target totalMs=3
```

## Revision (2026-07-06)

Addressed ClawSweeper review findings:

- **P1 — reload gap**: `updateConfig()` in heartbeat runner now calls `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` before rebuilding the agent schedule
- **P1 — override gap**: `requestHeartbeat()` wake handler pre-activates requested-heartbeat override targets before the no-bootstrap resolver runs
- **P1 — doctor regression**: `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` accepts `allowBootstrap?: boolean` so the doctor path (which runs outside the wake loop without preactivation) can still resolve external plugin targets
- **Test assertions**: `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts` now uses mocked `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin` with real assertions (call count, `allowBootstrap: true`, standard-channel skip, dedup)
- Kept existing `target:last` guarded bootstrap unchanged

## Revision (2026-07-07) #1

Removed duplicate heartbeat plugin preactivation path identified by ClawSweeper review:

- **P2 — duplicate startup preactivation**: Removed `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` from `activateGatewayScheduledServices`. The `startHeartbeatRunner` constructor already calls `updateConfig(state.cfg)` which handles the initial preactivation plus all hot-reload/config-update paths. Removing the gateway-side call eliminates a repeated registry scan when an external target fails to load.
- Updated comment in `heartbeat-runner.ts` `updateConfig` to reflect it is now the single preactivation path.
- 147 related tests pass (`server-runtime-services.test.ts`, `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts`, `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, `targets.test.ts`).

## Revision (2026-07-07) #2 (a0ba292)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P2] finding — gating preactivation to enabled, deliverable heartbeat configs:

**Problem**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` was called from `updateConfig` before the interval filter (`resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs`). A disabled heartbeat config (`every: "0m"`) with an external target still triggered `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` during startup/reload, scanning all installed plugins unnecessarily. External targets without a recipient (`to`) were also preactivated even though the runner can never deliver to them.

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- Config-scan path (startup/reload): each target is only preactivated when the heartbeat is enabled (`resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs` returns non-null) AND has a deliverable recipient (`to` is set). This mirrors the `updateConfig` scheduling loop which skips agents with `intervalMs === 0`.
- Direct heartbeat override path (cron/manual wakes via `requestHeartbeat`): still preactivates without an interval check because the caller already validated the wake is active. Only skips targets without a recipient.

**New regression tests** (+7 in `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`):
- ✅ Disabled default (`every: "0m"`) → no preactivation
- ✅ Disabled per-agent (`every: "0m"`) → no preactivation
- ✅ Missing `to` on default target → no preactivation
- ✅ Missing `to` on per-agent target → no preactivation
- ✅ Missing `to` on heartbeat override → no preactivation
- ✅ Per-agent with its own `every: "15m"` overrides disabled default → preactivated

**Test results**: 19/19 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 87/87 `targets.test.ts`, 25/25 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts` — all pass.

## Revision (2026-07-07) #3 (1334dd29)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P2] finding — skip default target preactivation when explicit per-agent heartbeats override scheduling:

**Problem**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` unconditionally added `agents.defaults.heartbeat` to the target set even when `agents.list[]` entries had their own heartbeat configs. In that case `resolveHeartbeatAgents` schedules only the merged per-agent entries — it does not schedule the default as a standalone target. Preactivating the unused default target caused an unnecessary full-plugin-registry scan on startup/reload.

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- Added a `hasExplicitAgents` check mirroring `resolveHeartbeatAgents`: when any `agents.list[]` entry has a `heartbeat` block, the standalone default target is skipped. Only the per-agent effective targets (which may merge `target` or `to` from defaults) are preactivated.
- When no agent has an explicit heartbeat, the default target is still preactivated as before (it is what the scheduler runs).

**Updated tests** (+1 new regression, 2 existing tests adjusted):
- ✅ New: "skips the default external target when a per-agent heartbeat overrides it" — default `unused-external-plugin` with `to: room:default` is not preactivated because agent `override-agent` has its own `background-channel` target
- ✅ Adjusted: "pre-activates distinct external targets from defaults and per-agent configs" → now expects only the per-agent target (default skipped)
- ✅ Adjusted: "pre-activates a per-agent external target that inherits to from defaults" → now expects only the per-agent target with inherited `to` (default skipped)

**Test results**: 21/21 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 87/87 `targets.test.ts`, 25/25 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts` — all pass (133 total).

## Revision (2026-07-07) #4 — fix external-target detector (9db74edf)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P1] finding — `isExternalPluginTarget` used wrong helper semantics:

**Problem**: `isExternalPluginTarget` used `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel()` and inverted its return value to decide "external plugin." But `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` preserves unknown plugin ids as deliverable (for external-plugin routing), so an explicit external target like `external-channel` made the helper return a truthy value and `isExternalPluginTarget` returned `false` — silently skipping bootstrap preactivation for external plugin targets.

**Root cause in the contract**:
- `normalizeMessageChannel` (in `message-channel-core.ts:27`) preserves unknown-but-normalized ids: `return normalizeAnyChannelId(normalized) ?? normalized`
- `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` wraps `normalizeMessageChannel` + `isDeliverableMessageChannel`, so it returns a truthy value for unknown external plugin channels
- The old `isExternalPluginTarget` inverted this: `return !normalized` — wrong, because the helper returned a value for external channels

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- Replaced `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` with `isDeliverableMessageChannel` + `normalizeChatChannelId`
- `isDeliverableMessageChannel(rawTarget)` confirms the target is a deliverable channel id (non-internal, non-empty)
- `!normalizeChatChannelId(rawTarget)` confirms it's NOT a built-in chat channel — built-in channels are already in the bundled catalog and don't need bootstrap
- Only targets that pass both checks (deliverable but not built-in) are classified as external plugin targets

**Updated tests** — `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`:
- Replaced `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` mock with `isDeliverableMessageChannel` + `normalizeChatChannelId` mocks
- `isDeliverableMessageChannel` now returns `true` for any non-empty string (matching real contract: unknown plugin ids are deliverable)
- `normalizeChatChannelId` only returns non-null for built-in channel ids (`telegram`, `discord`, `whatsapp`)
- This means external plugin targets (e.g. `external-channel`) correctly pass `isExternalPluginTarget` — deliverable but not built-in → needs preactivation
- Built-in channel targets (e.g. `telegram`) correctly fail `isExternalPluginTarget` — deliverable AND built-in → skip preactivation

**Test results**: 22/22 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 87/87 `targets.test.ts`, 27/27 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts` — all pass (136 total).



## Revision (2026-07-08)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P1] finding — explicit normalized heartbeat plugin targets not honoring caller `allowBootstrap`:

**Problem**: When `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` preserves an external plugin channel id (production normalization contract at `message-channel-core.ts:27-29`), the explicit target reaches the later plugin lookup at `targets.ts:217-225`. That lookup hardcoded `allowBootstrap: isSessionDerived` (always `false` for explicit targets) and `allowBundledFallback: !isSessionDerived` (always `true` for explicit targets). This meant:
- Doctor's `allowBootstrap: true` was ignored → false "replies are dropped silently" warnings for external plugin heartbeat targets
- Bundled fallback was enabled on the heartbeat hot path → could lazy-load bundled channel module code contrary to the performance boundary

**Fix in `targets.ts`**:
- `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget`: plugin lookup now honors `params.allowBootstrap` for explicit targets (`isSessionDerived || params.allowBootstrap === true`) and disables bundled fallback unconditionally (`allowBundledFallback: false`)
- `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTargetWithSessionRoute`: bundled fallback also disabled in sync with the primary resolution path

**New regression tests** (+2 in `targets.test.ts`):
- ✅ Doctor `allowBootstrap: true` passes through for explicit external targets preserved by production normalization
- ✅ Hot path keeps `allowBootstrap: false` with bundled fallback disabled
- Both tests override the normalization mock to simulate production behavior where external plugin ids are preserved (rather than returning `undefined`)

**Test results**: 89/89 `targets.test.ts`, 22/22 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 27/27 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts`, 7/7 `doctor-heartbeat-session-target.test.ts` — all pass (145 total).


## Revision (2026-07-08) #2 — fix CI lint (9a37f344)

Fixed `check-lint` CI failure (2 `eslint/curly` violations in `targets.test.ts`):

**Problem**: Two newly added test helpers in revision #1 used single-line `if (cond) return val;` without braces — a style rule enforced by `eslint/curly` in CI.

**Fix in `targets.test.ts`**: Added braces to both `if` statements (lines 987, 1026):
```ts
if (normalized === "ext-plugin") {
  return normalized;
}
```

**Test results**: 145/145 pass across 4 test files. `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean.


## Revision (2026-07-08) — external plugin proof

Real gateway proof with a minimal external channel plugin (`proof-channel`, `deliveryMode: "gateway"`, registered via `openclaw.plugin.json` `channels: ["proof-channel"]`). The plugin is NOT bundled — it lives under `~/.openclaw/extensions/proof-channel/` and is discovered at runtime.

### Setup

- Added `proof-channel` channel plugin to `~/.openclaw/extensions/proof-channel/` (CJS, `deliveryMode: "gateway"`, no bundled fallback)
- Configured `test_agent` with `heartbeat: { target: "proof-channel", to: "proof-test-recipient", every: "30s" }`
- Enabled `proof-channel` in `plugins.entries`
- Added temporary `appendFileSync` probes to capture the preactivation→delivery sequence (reverted before push)

### Gateway startup log

```
[gateway] loading configuration…
[gateway] resolving authentication…
[gateway] starting...
[gateway] starting HTTP server...
[health-monitor] started (interval: 300s, startup-grace: 60s, channel-connect-grace: 120s)
[plugins] proof-channel: loaded without install/load-path provenance; treat as untracked local code.
[heartbeat] started
```

### Proof event timeline

| Phase | Timestamp (UTC) | Event |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| Startup | `02:23:10.748Z` | `preactivate-start` — `hasOverride: false` (config-scan path) |
| Startup | `02:23:10.750Z` | `preactivate-config` — target=`proof-channel`, `targetCount=1`, calls `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` |
| Tick #1 | `02:23:22.678Z` | `heartbeat-delivery` — target=`proof-channel`, `allowBootstrap: false`, `pluginResolved: true`, `hadPreparedPlugin: false` |
| Tick #2 | `02:24:13.197Z` | `heartbeat-delivery` — target=`proof-channel`, `allowBootstrap: false`, `pluginResolved: true`, `hadPreparedPlugin: false` |

### Key observations

1. **Preactivation done once** — `preactivate-start` fires once at startup (config-scan path). The external plugin target `proof-channel` is resolved with `allowBootstrap: true`, loading it into the active registry.

2. **Hot path stays bootstrap-free** — Both heartbeat ticks deliver with `allowBootstrap: false`. The plugin is already active (`pluginResolved: true`) because preactivation loaded it.

3. **ZERO bootstrap-heavy events** — `bootstrapOutboundChannelPlugin` was never called on the hot path. The `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry` full-plugin-scan was never triggered during wake ticks. If the old `allowBootstrap: true` behavior were still in place, each tick would have triggered a full registry scan for this external plugin channel.

4. **No bundled fallback** — `hadPreparedPlugin: false` confirms delivery follows the explicit-target path, which disables `allowBundledFallback` — the bundled channel module code is never lazy-loaded from the heartbeat hot path.

### Environment

- OS: Linux (x86_64), Node 24.13.1
- Branch: `fix/heartbeat-delivery-bootstrap-latency`
- Commit: `9a37f344d49a7da5e182e750238885538aff5eed` (latest PR head)
- Config: production profile (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`) + proof plugin + heartbeat override
- Gateway port: 18790

### What was not tested

- Multi-agent heartbeat with mixed bundled/external targets
- Heartbeat delivery during plugin reload (`updateConfig` hot-reload path)
- Requested heartbeat override wake path (cron/manual wakes with external targets)
- Production external plugins (qqbot, feishu) — proof used a minimal no-network plugin to isolate the registry/preactivation behavior



## Revision (2026-07-08) — normalize target before preactivation classification (d5b03d3)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P1] finding — `isExternalPluginTarget` checked raw heartbeat target with `isDeliverableMessageChannel` without prior normalization:

**Problem**: Config validation accepts heartbeat targets case-insensitively by lowercasing installed plugin channel ids before membership checks (`src/config/validation.ts:1765`). A config `target: "Proof-Channel"` passes validation and delivery later normalizes it to `proof-channel`, but `isDeliverableMessageChannel("Proof-Channel")` returns `false` (it requires already-normalized input per `message-channel-core.ts:36`). The un-normalized mixed-case target was silently skipped, leaving the external plugin un-preloaded — the no-bootstrap hot path then resolved to no target.

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- `isExternalPluginTarget` now normalizes the raw target via `normalizeMessageChannel` before calling `isDeliverableMessageChannel` and `normalizeChatChannelId`. This mirrors the config validation contract where installed plugin channel ids are lowercased.
- Imported `normalizeMessageChannel` from `../../utils/message-channel.js` alongside the existing `isDeliverableMessageChannel`.

**New regression test** (+1 in `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`):
- ✅ "pre-activates a mixed-case external plugin target" — `target: "Proof-Channel"` is normalized to `proof-channel`, classified as external, and resolved with `allowBootstrap: true`
- Added `normalizeMessageChannel` mock that lowercases input, matching the production contract

**Test results**: 23/23 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 89/89 `targets.test.ts`, 27/27 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts`, 7/7 `doctor-heartbeat-session-target.test.ts` — all pass (146 total). `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean.

target.body:
## Summary
- parse one-shot `autostart` from Control UI/WebChat URLs and strip it after capture
- defer captured autostart requests while a gateway URL confirmation is pending
- run the bootstrap prompt only after an empty `chat.history` load succeeds
- send autostart through the chat controller as a hidden, no-local-echo prompt with stable idempotency

## Dependency
Draft until #79652 lands. This UI path relies on the `chat.send.hideUserMessage` Gateway protocol flag added there.

## Why
This keeps the URL/autostart behavior separate from the Gateway protocol change so reviewers can inspect the browser flow without also reviewing the server-side hidden-send authorization path.

## Real behavior proof
- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Control UI/WebChat deep links can stage a one-shot bootstrap prompt that becomes a hidden `chat.send` request after an empty `chat.history` load, without leaving the triggering bootstrap prompt in chat history.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS source checkout using the split UI branch with the dependent Gateway behavior from #79652, foreground OpenClaw Gateway on `ws://127.0.0.1:19886` with token auth and `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Verified the UI URL capture/autostart dispatch path with the targeted browser-controller tests below, then ran the resulting hidden Gateway request shape against a real local Gateway: `chat.history`, `chat.send` with `{ "sessionKey": "main", "message": "/context list", "hideUserMessage": true }`, and `chat.history` again.
- **Evidence after fix**: Terminal output from the live local gateway client run of the hidden request emitted by the UI autostart path:

```json
{
  "connected": true,
  "url": "ws://127.0.0.1:19886",
  "before": {
    "sessionId": null,
    "messageCount": 0,
    "texts": []
  },
  "send": {
    "runId": "proof-hidden-send-1778301902610",
    "status": "started"
  },
  "after": {
    "sessionId": "933b48d9-d050-4337-b09f-291cd535db91",
    "messageCount": 0,
    "texts": [],
    "containsHiddenPrompt": false
  }
}
```

- **Observed result after fix**: The real gateway accepted the hidden send shape used by autostart, returned a backing `sessionId`, and did not expose the hidden bootstrap trigger in chat history. The UI tests verify URL stripping, pending-gateway deferral, empty-history gating, stable idempotency, and no local user echo.
- **What was not tested**: Full manual browser screenshot of the URL flow; this PR remains draft until the dependent Gateway PR #79652 lands.

## Testing
- `pnpm test ui/src/ui/controllers/chat.test.ts ui/src/ui/app-settings.test.ts ui/src/ui/app-chat.test.ts -t "omits hideUserMessage for normal chat sends|can send a hidden prompt without local echoing the user turn|reuses a caller-provided idempotency key|does not inject an orphaned assistant error|captures and strips autostart prompts from the URL|autostarts a hidden prompt once for an empty chat session|skips autostart when chat history failed to load|preserves autostart when the hidden send fails|clears session binding after a successful hidden send"`

target.title: fix(telegram): keep DM topic auto-rename user message UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who send long Telegram messages containing emoji as their first turn in a DM topic session would get a garbled or empty auto-renamed topic title.

OpenClaw can automatically rename Telegram forum topics on the first turn of a session. To do this it truncates the user's message to 500 characters and passes it to an LLM for label generation. The truncation uses `.slice(0, 500)`, which counts UTF-16 code units. Emoji and other characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane are represented as surrogate pairs (two UTF-16 code units). If such a character straddles the 500-unit boundary, the slice discards the second half of the pair, producing an isolated high surrogate — invalid Unicode.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `.slice(0, 500)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(..., 500)`, which backs up one code unit when the cut point falls inside a surrogate pair. This helper is the established pattern for all user-text truncation in the codebase (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`).

## User Impact

Users sending emoji-heavy first messages in Telegram DM topic sessions (e.g. `"Hi 👋 tell me about 🦞🦞🦞 …"` long enough to reach 500 chars) would receive a malformed auto-topic label — either a replacement character, garbled output, or a rejected model call. After this fix the topic label is always derived from a valid Unicode string.

## Evidence

- **Affected path:** `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts:3078` — `userMessage` is built with `truncateUtf16Safe(ctxPayload.RawBody ?? ctxPayload.Body ?? "", 500)` then passed to `generateTopicLabel({ userMessage, … })`.
- **Fix:** `truncateUtf16Safe(..., 500)` — same semantics, surrogate-safe boundary.
- **Pattern match:** `truncateUtf16Safe` is used in the same way throughout the Telegram plugin for other string limits (e.g. `raw-update-log.ts`) and was added for exactly this class of bug.
- **Diff:** one new import, one call-site replacement in `bot-message-dispatch.ts`; surrogate-boundary regression in `bot-message-dispatch.test.ts`.

### Behavior proof

#### 1) Node runtime boundary reproduction (exact `bot-message-dispatch.ts` expression, no mocks)

Uses the same input shape as the regression test (`499 × 'a' + 😀tail`) and the production truncation expression:

```text
=== Telegram DM topic auto-rename UTF-16 reproduction (Node runtime, bot-message-dispatch.ts logic, no mocks) ===
Node: v22.22.0
rawBody code units: 505
old .slice(0, 500) code units: 500
old userMessage has unpaired surrogate: true
old userMessage last char: U+D83D
truncateUtf16Safe(rawBody, 500) code units: 499
fixed userMessage has unpaired surrogate: false
fixed userMessage equals 499 ASCII a's: true
fixed userMessage would reach generateTopicLabel cleanly: true
```

This shows the before/after contract on the auto-topic label input path: emoji straddling the 500 cap is dropped whole instead of leaving `U+D83D` in `userMessage`.

#### 2) Call-site regression through production `dispatchTelegramMessage`

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts -t "truncates DM topic auto-rename" --reporter=verbose

 ✓ dispatchTelegramMessage draft streaming > truncates DM topic auto-rename input on UTF-16 boundaries

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 171 skipped (172)
```

Regression drives the real DM-topic auto-rename branch and asserts `generateTopicLabel` receives `userMessage` with length ≤ 500, no unpaired surrogate, and value exactly `499 × 'a'` for boundary input `499 × 'a' + 😀tail`.

**Proof gap:** No redacted live Telegram Desktop / Bot API transcript in this validation environment. Node reproduction plus the `dispatchTelegramMessage` regression cover the production truncation before `generateTopicLabel`; optional supplemental proof is a redacted first-turn DM topic rename showing a long emoji-near-boundary message produces a well-formed topic title.

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor / Claude Sonnet 4.6)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

target.title: fix(googlechat): cap approval binding registries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two unbounded in-process Maps in the Google Chat approval flow:

1. **`approvalCardBindings`** — maps approval tokens to in-flight native Google Chat interactive card state. No eviction path; on a long-lived gateway with high approval-card throughput this Map grows without limit.
2. **`manualApprovalFollowupSuppressions`** — tracks approval IDs to suppress duplicate follow-up text after native card delivery. Same unbounded growth pattern.

## Why This Change Was Made

Applies `pruneMapToMaxSize` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime` immediately after every `.set` call on both Maps, each capped at **1 024 entries** with LRU eviction. An evicted binding simply cannot be resolved — the same behavior as a gateway restart.

## User Impact

Operators running Google Chat channels with high approval-card volume on long-lived gateways get bounded memory for both registries. Behavior is unchanged for the first 1 024 simultaneous in-flight approval cards.

## Evidence

- `extensions/googlechat/src/approval-card-actions.ts:27–30` — module-level `approvalCardBindings` and `manualApprovalFollowupSuppressions` Maps
- `extensions/googlechat/src/approval-card-actions.ts:123,170–173` — `pruneMapToMaxSize` after each `.set`
- `src/infra/map-size.ts` — shared `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper re-exported via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`
- Diff: production changes in `approval-card-actions.ts`; regressions in `approval-card-actions.test.ts`

### Behavior proof

#### 1) Node runtime through production registry exports (no Vitest mocks)

Imports and exercises the real `registerGoogleChatApprovalCardBinding`, `getGoogleChatApprovalCardBinding`, `registerGoogleChatManualApprovalFollowupSuppression`, and `shouldSuppressGoogleChatManualExecApprovalFollowupText` helpers from `approval-card-actions.ts`:

```text
=== Google Chat approval registry cap proof (Node runtime, production exports, no Vitest) ===
Node: v22.22.0

[approvalCardBindings] after first register: resolvable=true
after 1025 total registers:
  oldest token-first evicted: true
  newest token-fill-1024 retained: true

[manualApprovalFollowupSuppressions] after 1025 registers:
  oldest first approval suppressed before fill: true
  oldest first approval suppressed after fill: false
  newest 1024-padded approval suppressed: true
```

Space names redacted. This shows both registries stay bounded at 1024 entries and evict oldest insertion-order records once the cap is exceeded.

#### 2) Call-site regression tests

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/googlechat/src/approval-card-actions.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ evicts oldest approval card bindings once the cache exceeds its cap
 ✓ evicts oldest manual approval follow-up suppressions once the cache exceeds its cap

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

Regressions register 1 025 entries and confirm:
- oldest approval-card token `token-first` becomes unresolvable while `token-fill-1024` remains resolvable
- oldest manual follow-up suppression stops matching while the newest padded approval ID still suppresses

**Proof gap:** No redacted live Google Chat native approval-card delivery or button-click transcript in this validation environment. Node runtime plus registry regressions cover the production in-process Maps; optional supplemental proof is a redacted gateway log showing approval-card registration under sustained throughput with stable memory.

target.title: fix(gateway): cap pendingFinalDelivery retries and prevent delivery wedge
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway restart while a final reply was pending could wedge that delivery forever. Restart recovery replayed stale `pendingFinalDelivery` payloads with no cap and no backoff, and a payload that a downstream route never cleared was replayed on every subsequent restart. This PR bounds that recovery:

- Recent attempts back off exponentially (30s base, 30 min ceiling) and payloads are dead-lettered after 10 recovery attempts by default, clearing the pending-final and restart-recovery fields so the session no longer stays restart-recoverable forever.
- Future persisted `pendingFinalDeliveryLastAttemptAt` values are treated as no active backoff, so clock skew, VM resume, or NTP correction cannot preserve the wedge.
- Backoff-deferred entries are surfaced from `recoverStore` as a closed `deferred` shape (count plus earliest `nextEligibleAtMs`), and the startup scheduler runs one bounded follow-up recovery pass when the earliest backoff expires. This addresses the ClawSweeper P1: previously a backoff-active entry only counted as skipped and the scheduler re-queued only on `failed > 0`, so the entry waited for the next gateway restart. Follow-up passes do not consume the failed-retry budget and are naturally bounded by the per-entry attempt cap (dead-letter) and the backoff ceiling.
- The cap is threaded through the restart recovery entry points so tests and callers can tune it.

## Context

This follows up on #92082 and the July 5, 2026 restart incident where pending final delivery state was part of the delivery wedge investigation. Current `main` already carries the v2026.6.5 fixes for bounded heartbeat scheduling and preserved delivery context; this patch closes the remaining startup-recovery path that could keep replaying a durable pending final across gateway restarts.

The Telegram ingress fixes requested alongside this work (#93281, #96962, #97118) are already ancestors of current `main`, so there was no scoped upstream backport diff to open for that part.

## Evidence

All commands run on `37fb71f5b07067f4023527a8d3e3667f9bd155c8` (rebased on current `main` 827f2c44225e):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts` — 1 file, 38 tests passed, including the new scheduler-level regression: a pending final inside backoff is retried after expiry without a restart (fake timers drive the scheduler; the resume fires only after the 60s attempt-2 backoff elapses).
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts` — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- `pnpm build` — full build green (tsdown + postbuild + plugin assets).

Live restart-recovery proof, re-run after the scheduler fix: an isolated Node process imported the rebuilt `dist` recovery module with a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and a localhost-only minimal fake gateway (connect challenge + hello-ok + `agent` acceptor). Seeded one pending final at `attemptCount=1` with `lastAttemptAt` 25s old (30s backoff, eligible in ~5s), then called `scheduleRestartAbortedMainSessionRecovery`. The production gateway was not restarted or contacted. Redacted output:

```text
PROOF phase=schedule start attemptCount=1 lastAttemptAt=25s-old backoff=30s eligibleIn~5s port=65180
[main-session-restart-recovery] pending final delivery restart recovery backoff active for agent:main:proof-pending-final after 1/10 attempts
PROOF phase=deferred result acceptedAgentRequests=0 persistedAttemptCount=1 abortedLastRun=true
PROOF fake-gateway accepted agent request #1
[main-session-restart-recovery] resumed interrupted main session: agent:main:proof-pending-final (with pending payload)
[main-session-restart-recovery] main-session restart recovery complete: recovered=1 failed=0 skipped=0
PROOF phase=follow-up result acceptedAgentRequests=1 persistedAttemptCount=2 abortedLastRun=false pendingFinalDelivery=true
PROOF verdict=PASS
```

The deferred entry was not retried by the first pass, and the scheduler's follow-up pass retried it in-process once the backoff expired: attempt count 1 -> 2, `abortedLastRun` cleared, exactly one `agent` request accepted.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: a pending final delivery inside its restart-recovery backoff window was never retried in the same process because the startup scheduler only re-queued failed passes; it stayed wedged until the next gateway restart.
- Real environment tested: macOS (Darwin 25.5.0), Node 26.4.0, isolated Node process driving the rebuilt `dist` recovery module from this branch with a temp state dir and a localhost-only fake gateway; no production gateway involved.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: seeded `sessions.json` with `pendingFinalDelivery=true`, `pendingFinalDeliveryAttemptCount=1`, `pendingFinalDeliveryLastAttemptAt` 25s old; ran `scheduleRestartAbortedMainSessionRecovery({ stateDir, delayMs: 200 })` from `dist/main-session-restart-recovery-*.js`; also ran `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts`.
- Evidence after fix: redacted live output above (`PROOF verdict=PASS`) plus vitest `Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 38 passed (38)`.
- Observed result after fix: first recovery pass deferred the backoff-active entry without calling the gateway; the scheduled follow-up pass fired after backoff expiry, the fake gateway accepted exactly one `agent` retry, and the store showed `pendingFinalDeliveryAttemptCount` 1 -> 2 with `abortedLastRun=false`.
- What was not tested: live gateway restart-recovery soak on upstream main.

target.title: fix(nextcloud-talk): add timeouts to Talk send requests
target.body:
Related: #95865

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users sending Nextcloud Talk messages or reactions could have the send workflow wait indefinitely when the Talk server accepts the HTTP connection but never responds.

## Why This Change Was Made

Nextcloud Talk's preflight path already passes a request timeout into `fetchWithSsrFGuard`; this change applies the same bounded request behavior to message and reaction sends while preserving the existing SSRF policy, headers, and response handling.

## User Impact

Operators get a bounded failure instead of a stuck outbound send when a self-hosted or remote Talk endpoint hangs after accepting the connection.

## Evidence

- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/send.fetch-timeout.test.ts` - passed; `Test Files  1 passed (1)`, `Tests  2 passed (2)`.
- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/send.ts extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/send.fetch-timeout.test.ts` - passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` - passed; exit 0.
- Mutation check: temporarily removing the two `timeoutMs` guard parameters made the focused Vitest fail with `2 failed` and `expected 'pending' to be 'rejected'` for both message and reaction paths; restoring the patch returned the test to green.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Nextcloud Talk message and reaction POSTs now have a deadline when the remote server accepts the request but never sends a response.

Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout; real `node:http` loopback server that accepts the connection and never responds, driving the real exported `sendMessageNextcloudTalk` and `sendReactionNextcloudTalk` functions.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/send.fetch-timeout.test.ts`

Evidence after fix: the focused test asserts the real loopback server receives the outbound message and reaction POSTs; without the timeout wiring the calls remain pending past the race window, and with the patch they reject with an abort/timeout-class error.

Observed result after fix: `Test Files  1 passed (1)` and `Tests  2 passed (2)`.

What was not tested: a live Nextcloud Talk endpoint; the hang is reproduced with a real local HTTP server, not the real third-party service.
